_readme: THE BOX ITSELF — which tenants this bench has, which stores live in each, and the instance settings every
screen inherits. Applied by `bin/seed-box.mjs`, ONE TENANT PER RUN (the write face takes the tenant as a
header, so a run is scoped to one by construction).
★ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS INSTEAD OF `stores` IN `catalog.json`. That list has NO TENANT AXIS — it is a flat
array from the days this bench had one tenant, and it cannot say which of two tenants a store belongs to.
The topology it could not express is now the point: two brands, four stores, one admin container. So the
TERRAIN (tenants, stores, settings) is declared here and the CATALOGUE stays over there.
⚠️ `catalog.json` STILL CARRIES A `stores` ARRAY and it is now SUPERSEDED. It is not deleted here because
that file is being restructured by another slice in this same wave, and two hands in one file is how a
merge eats a decision. Until it goes, `bin/seed.mjs` may still create a store from it — which is
IDEMPOTENT (it skips a handle that exists) but would put it in whichever tenant that run is pointed at.
Point that script at the right tenant, or let this one run first.
★ `require_shipping_document` LIVES HERE FOR A REASON WORTH READING. It is what makes the shipping
widget grow its fiscal block, and it used to be switched on at the end of a LOGISTICS function inside the
history executor. It is tenant configuration, like the three settings beside it, and tenant configuration
written by a data seeder is the thing that surprises somebody in three months looking for where it was
turned on. Same reason the currency is declared even though it is already the default: the place a switch
is declared should be the place a reader would look for it.
★★ `dataset` — WHOSE CATALOGUE THE MOUNTED EXAMPLE DATA IS, AND IT IS THE FIELD THIS FILE EXISTS
TO CARRY. A box mounts ONE example dataset (`FORGE_SEED_DATASET_DIR`), and a dataset is a BRAND's: this
one is the footwear catalogue. `dist/seed-demo.js` fills the tenant it is POINTED AT — correctly, from
whatever dataset is mounted — so pointing it at a second tenant fills a coffee shop with shoes. Measured
on the bench of 02/09: `forgecafe` held 2 811 products (21 curated + the dataset's 2 790), 44 490 SKUs,
351 footwear brands and the dataset's eleven footwear custom fields. The kernel did nothing wrong — the
same handles carry DIFFERENT ids in the two schemas, so those were two correctly-scoped writes, not a
leak. The defect was `bin/box-up.sh` running step 9 `for t in $TENANTS`. This field is what it reads now.
★ AND THE TENANT THAT DOES NOT CARRY IT NEEDS THE OTHER HALF OF THAT ONE-SHOT. `seed-demo.js` fuses two
jobs: fill the store from the dataset, and PROVISION the tenant (its apps, its delivery, its checkout
flags). Only the first is the dataset's. So a `dataset: false` tenant declares `apps` and `delivery`
here, `bin/seed-box.mjs` applies them at step 6, and the tenant stands without borrowing another brand's
catalogue. ⚠️ A `dataset: true` tenant must NOT declare them — the one-shot is their owner, and two
owners for one gesture is how this repository has already grown a duplicate.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, and deliberately: the FIRST store of each tenant. `provision-ref` creates it at
bootstrap (`FORGE_REF_STORE_HANDLE`), before any credential exists to drive the port with — so listing it
here would be a second author for a row that already has one. It is named below only so a reader can see
the whole shape, with `bootstrap: true` marking who really makes it.

tenants.why: T1, the footwear brand. The tenant this bench was born with, kept under its own name so nothing that already refers to it has to move.
tenants._dataset_why: The mounted example data IS this brand's catalogue — 2 790 footwear products, 351 footwear brands, and the footwear facet vocabulary in its `custom-fields.json`. So step 9 of `bin/box-up.sh` runs here, and everything it brings (the catalogue, the storefront apps, the delivery methods, the checkout flags) has one owner: the one-shot.

stores.name: Forge
stores.why: The reference storefront, unforked and unthemed. It is the control: every other store's thesis is that a theme plus data plus composition is enough, and a thesis needs something to be compared against.

stores.name: Forge Outlet
stores.why: The same catalogue under a theme of its own. Second store of T1, created through the port.

tenants.why: T2, the coffee business. A SECOND TENANT, which this bench never had — and the thing that makes it possible is not a second admin container: `read.admin.by_host` resolves the tenant from the request's host:port and `platform.admin_host.set` writes that map, so one admin serves both.
tenants._dataset_why: A coffee business is not the brand the mounted example data describes. Its catalogue is the CURATED one this repository writes — 6 coffees + the counter's 15 — and nothing else belongs in it. Step 9 therefore does not run here; `apps` and `delivery` below are the half of that one-shot this tenant really did need.
_apps_why: THE APPS STEP 9 USED TO INSTALL HERE AS A SIDE EFFECT OF FILLING A CATALOGUE THIS TENANT SHOULD NEVER
HAVE HAD. Measured on the bench of 02/09 (`forge_control.extension_installation`): these six landed in
`forgecafe` at 00:59:41, inside `seedCuratedStorefront` — the second half of the dataset one-shot.
`reviews` and `subscriptions` are NOT here and must not be: `seed/coffee.mjs` installs those, and one
gesture may only have one owner.
⚠️ `payment-reference` and `payment-mercadopago` are why a coffee cart can be paid at all — a store with
no payment app reaches the payment step with no method, which is a dead end that reads as a broken
checkout. `admin-dashboard` is what puts the three widgets on this tenant's admin home.
_delivery_why: A COFFEE SHOP THAT DELIVERS NEEDS ITS OWN FREIGHT, and until now it borrowed the footwear seeder's. Same
two methods and the same figures `demo-data`'s `populate` writes — deliberately, so nothing a human has
already tested changes shape — but declared HERE, by the box, for the tenant that owns them.
⛔ IT IS ALSO A PRECONDITION OF STEP 10, NOT A GARNISH. `seed-history` refuses a tenant with more than one
active delivery method, and box-up silences all but the one named by $FORGE_HISTORY_KEEP_METHOD
("Entrega Padrão") — a tenant with NO delivery method fails that step by name. So this is applied at
step 6, before the curated seed, the past and the window: exactly where `bin/seed-box.mjs` runs.
⚠️ TENANT-WIDE, no `store_id` — the same limitation `seed/totem.json` writes up for the counter's pickup:
these commands have no store axis, so the counter's checkout sees these two as well.

stores.name: Forge Café
stores._masked_checkout_why: A RECOGNISED BUYER SKIPS RE-TYPING WHAT THE SHOP ALREADY KNOWS. Born OFF (the column's default), and until now it was flipped ON by `configureStore` inside the dataset one-shot — the same step 9 this tenant no longer runs. Declared here so the coffee shop keeps the checkout a human already tested. The counter does not declare it: a totem has no returning session to recognise.
stores.why: The coffee e-commerce, on its forked storefront. Born in T2 rather than moved into it: data does not travel sideways between tenants, so on a virgin box this is simply where it is created.

stores.name: Forge Café · Balcão
stores.why: The counter the totem serves. No `theme_key` on purpose: the totem is an app of its own and resolves no theme, so a theme key here would be a promise nothing keeps. Same tenant as `cafe` — one catalogue, two assortments.
